name: model-sweep-demo
notes: The 'compare many models' cookbook, built from pieces that already exist: SklearnFit is a DOORWAY (the estimator is named by the document, not by a wrapper class), and `estimator` is one of its declared params, so an ordinary search space over `model.estimator` IS the model sweep. There are no per-model classes anywhere in this document or in the pack — adding a candidate is one more string in the list below. Run: python -m dskit.pipeline run examples/pipeline/model-sweep.json --asof 2026-01-01

dataset.notes: role 'data': deterministic settled events with a mid that under-reacts to the truth. Swap this node for your own data source and the sweep below is unchanged — the candidates never mention the domain.

model.notes: The estimator named here is the BASE pass; the sweep overrides it per trial, so this value is only the fallback the document runs with when nobody searches. `estimator_params` is deliberately absent: one params block serves every candidate, so it may carry only knobs they ALL accept (a constructor kwarg one candidate has never heard of is refused by that candidate at fit time). `seed` is absent for the same reason — SklearnFit refuses a seed the estimator would never read, and LinearRegression/SVR/KNeighbors take no random_state, so the forest here is unseeded on purpose. To tune ONE model's hyperparameters instead, pin `estimator` and put its own knobs in the space (e.g. 'model.estimator_params.alpha').

validate.notes: The comparison metric — the ONE criterion every candidate is judged by, declared here rather than hidden inside a framework. Selection reads the val split only; the planner refuses a search whose objective comes from train or test.

sweep.notes: The estimator LIST is config, not code — this is the whole 'sweep the common models' feature. Exhaustive by default (no n_trials): 6 candidates, 6 trials, one fit each, then the winner is re-applied so downstream consumes the tuned pass. The list is sklearn-only ON PURPOSE so this example runs on dskit[sklearn] alone; boosted-tree libraries with an sklearn-compatible API drop straight in once installed — add 'lightgbm.LGBMRegressor' (pip install 'dskit[lightgbm]') beside these, and xgboost/catboost the same way. Spelling: SklearnFit takes a DOTTED import path (module.ClassName); 'lightgbm:LGBMRegressor' with a colon is refused at plan. Swap `uses` to 'dskit.pipeline.libs.optuna:OptunaSearch' for TPE sampling over the same list.

report.notes: downstream of the search: consumes the winner pass, so `loss` is the WINNING model's val loss, not the base pass's
